_what: Every claim that Gavril APPROVED something, with the VERBATIM QUOTE and the exact SCOPE of what the quote covers. Nothing else in this repo may cite 'approved' as provenance without pointing at an id in here.
_why: 2026-08-05. He corrected me: 'no i did not approve number 3 i just approved one of the scene inside'. I had written that he approved a whole video when what he said was that he liked ONE SCENE in it, and I had then used that inflated approval as ground truth to justify a constant. His eye is the ONLY ground truth this system has - every metric I own is validated against it - so inflating the scope of an approval quietly forges the warrant for everything downstream. An audit found the word 'approved' 13 times in the repo and most could not produce the quote that earned it.
_rule: An approval record needs three things or it is not an approval: (1) the VERBATIM words, (2) the SCOPE - what exactly the words cover, which is almost always narrower than the artefact, (3) what it does NOT cover. 'He approved X' with no quote is banned. A partial positive ('I like the sunset scene') is a SCENE-level approval and may never be promoted to an artefact-level one.
_asymmetry: Approval scope inflation is worse than under-recording, because a constant justified by a false approval will not be re-examined - it looks settled. Under-recording only costs a question.
